answer: An agent economy can tax identity itself by pricing the height of the attestation graph. Each newcomer climbs from its own cedar root upward, and the reward it earns decays with every shared ancestor it holds with a neighbour: a farm of a thousand shells planted beside one knoll pays far less per head than a thousand genuinely distant agents. The kernel of the rule is that cloning concentrates lineage, so sybil cost grows super-linearly while honest diversity still pays.
